{{Short description|Czech-Australian astrophysicist}}
{{EngvarB|date=September 2014}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2014}}
'''Pavel Kroupa''' (born 24 September 1963, [[Jindřichův Hradec]], Czechoslovakia) is a Czech-Australian [[astrophysicist]] and professor at the [[University of Bonn]], Germany, where he holds a position at the Helmholtz-Institut für Strahlen- und Kernphysik (HISKP). He also holds an affiliation with the Astronomical Institute of [[Charles University]] in Prague, where he was named Professorem Hospitem in 2017.<ref name="hiskp">Helmholtz-Institut für Strahlen- und Kernphysik, University of Bonn. http://www.iskp.uni-bonn.de</ref><ref name="praguehospitem">Kroupa, Pavel. "Professorem Hospitem, Charles University." https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/Prof_Hospitem.html</ref>

Kroupa leads the Stellar Populations and Dynamics Research (SPODYR) group. He is internationally recognised for his foundational contributions to the theory of the stellar [[initial mass function]] (IMF), the dynamics of [[binary star]] systems and [[star cluster]]s, the Integrated Galactic Initial Mass Function (IGIMF) theory, and for his research critically examining the standard [[Lambda-CDM model|ΛCDM]] cosmological model and exploring [[Milgromian dynamics]] (MOND) as an alternative framework.<ref name="spodyr">SPODYR Group, University of Bonn. https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/resea.html</ref><ref name="darkmattercrisis">Kroupa, P. (2012). "The Dark Matter Crisis." ''PASA'', 29, 395. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012PASA...29..395K</ref>

He is the author of 389 refereed publications cited more than 32,800 times, with an h-index of 84 as of March 2026.<ref name="cv">Kroupa, Pavel. Curriculum Vitae (March 2026) — Publications and grants summary. https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/life.html</ref> In 2024 he was listed among the top-ranked scholars of all time across all fields by ScholarGPS, as the top scholar at Charles University in Prague and sixth at the University of Bonn.<ref name="scholargps">ScholarGPS. "Pavel Kroupa — Highly Ranked Scholar." 2024. https://scholargps.com/scholars/72047389554791/pavel-kroupa</ref>

==Early Life and Background==

Kroupa was born on 24 September 1963 in [[Jindřichův Hradec]], Czechoslovakia. When the [[Prague Spring]] failed in August 1968 and Warsaw Pact forces invaded, his father fled the country with him on the first night of the invasion.<ref name="lifestations">Kroupa, Pavel. "Life's Stations and Career Synopsis." https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/life.html</ref>

The family subsequently lived in: Kassel, West Germany (1968–1972); Pretoria, South Africa (1972–1977); Göttingen, West Germany (1977–1983); and Perth, Western Australia (1983–1988).<ref name="lifestationslist">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Life's Stations list. https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/life.html</ref> He attended the Christian Brothers' Catholic School in Pretoria and the Theodor-Heuss-Gymnasium in Göttingen, the latter until 1983.<ref name="gymnasium">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Theodor-Heuss-Gymnasium, Göttingen. https://astro.uni-bonn.de/~pavel/life.html</ref>

Kroupa holds dual Australian and Czech citizenship.<ref name="lifestations"/>

==Education==

Kroupa commenced physics studies at the [[University of Western Australia]] (UWA), Perth, in 1984. In 1986–87 he held a Summer Vacation Scholarship at [[Mount Stromlo Observatory]], [[Australian National University]], Canberra.<ref name="anu">Kroupa, Pavel. CV (March 2026) — 1986/87 Summer Vacation Scholarship, ANU.</ref> He graduated in 1988 with a first-class BSc (Honours) in physics from UWA, supervised by Dr. David Blair and Dr. Ron Burman.<ref name="pasa1989">Kroupa, P., Burman, R.R., Blair, D.G. (1989). ''PASA'' 8, 119. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1989PASAu...8..119K</ref>

In 1988 he was awarded an Isaac Newton Studentship by the [[University of Cambridge]] and selected for membership at [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]]. He commenced his PhD in astrophysics at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]], supervised by Dr. Gerard F. Gilmore, with Christopher A. Tout as mentor. In January–March 1991 he was a Visiting Research Fellow at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]]. In October 1991 he was awarded the Senior Rouse Ball Research Studentship by Trinity College.<ref name="cambridge">Kroupa, Pavel. CV (March 2026) — Isaac Newton Studentship and Senior Rouse Ball Scholarship, Trinity College Cambridge.</ref>

He successfully defended his PhD thesis, ''The distribution of low-mass stars in the Galactic disc'', at Cambridge in May 1992.<ref name="phdthesis">Kroupa, Pavel. PhD thesis: ''The distribution of low-mass stars in the Galactic disc''. University of Cambridge, 1992.</ref>

In 2002 he earned his [[Habilitation]] at [[Kiel University]] with the thesis ''Binary Systems, Star Clusters and the Galactic-Field Population''.<ref name="habilitation">Kroupa, Pavel. Habilitation thesis: ''Binary systems, star clusters and the galactic-field population''. Kiel University, 2002.</ref>

==Academic Career==

===Heidelberg (1992–2000)===

Following his doctorate, Kroupa took up a five-year research appointment at the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut (ARI), Heidelberg, under Prof. Dr. Roland Wielen. In 1997 he moved to the Institut für Theoretische Astrophysik, University of Heidelberg, under Prof. Dr. Werner Tscharnuter, and subsequently spent periods at the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Astronomie]] (MPIA).<ref name="heidelberg">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Heidelberg postdoctoral positions 1992–2000 (ARI, MPIA, ITA).</ref> In March–July 1999 he was a Smithsonian Short-Term Visitor at the [[Harvard–Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]].<ref name="smithsonian">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Smithsonian Short-Term Visitor, Harvard-Smithsonian CfA, 1999.</ref>

===Kiel University (2000–2004)===

In November 2000 Kroupa moved to [[Kiel University]]. He completed his Habilitation there in 2002 and was awarded a five-year Heisenberg Fellowship by the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] in November 2002.<ref name="kiel">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Heisenberg Fellowship, DFG, November 2002.</ref>

===University of Bonn (2004–present)===

In April 2004 Kroupa was appointed professor of astronomy at the Sternwarte der Universität Bonn (since 2006 part of the [[Argelander Institute for Astronomy|Argelander-Institut für Astronomie]], AIfA). In October 2013 he transferred to the HISKP at the University of Bonn.<ref name="bonn">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Transfer to HISKP, 1 October 2013; Bonn professorship from April 2004.</ref> In 2012 he was elected Managing Director of the AIfA for one academic year.<ref name="aifa">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Elected Managing Director, AIfA, October 2012.</ref> In 2023 he was appointed Equal Opportunities Officer (Gleichstellungsbeauftragter) at the University of Bonn.<ref name="scholargps"/>

===Charles University in Prague (2016–present)===

From 1 August 2016, Kroupa took up an affiliation with the Astronomical Institute of [[Charles University]] in Prague. On 3 May 2017 he was named Professorem Hospitem by the Rector of Charles University.<ref name="praguehospitem"/><ref name="pragueaffiliation">Kroupa, Pavel. CV — Affiliation with Charles University from 1 August 2016.</ref>

==Research==

===Initial Mass Function===

Kroupa's most widely cited work concerns the stellar [[initial mass function]] (IMF). Working in Cambridge (1990–1992) with Christopher A. Tout and Gerard F. Gilmore, he analysed star count and binary star data, incorporating advanced physics of the stellar mass-luminosity relation and corrections for unresolved binary systems and a Galactic field model. This work yielded what became known as the canonical IMF — a two-part [[power law|power-law]] form.<ref name="ktg1993">Kroupa, P., Tout, C.A., Gilmore, G. (1993). ''MNRAS'', 262, 545. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1993MNRAS.262..545K</ref>

The papers Kroupa, Tout & Gilmore (1993) and Kroupa (2001) have together received more than 7,843 citations.<ref name="cv"/> The 2002 ''Science'' paper "The Initial Mass Function of Stars: Evidence for Uniformity in Variable Systems" was published as an invited review.<ref name="science2002">Kroupa, P. (2002). ''Science'', 295, 82. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002Sci...295...82K</ref>

===IGIMF Theory===

In 2003 Kroupa and later PhD student Carsten Weidner introduced the Integrated Galactic Initial Mass Function (IGIMF) Theory, a framework for calculating the galaxy-wide stellar IMF from its constituent embedded star clusters.<ref name="igimf">Kroupa, P., Weidner, C. (2003). ''ApJ'', 598, 1076. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003ApJ...598.1076K/abstract</ref>

The theory predicts that the galaxy-wide IMF differs systematically from the IMF of individual clusters, with proposed consequences including:

* Star-forming [[Dwarf galaxy|dwarf galaxies]] being [[H-alpha|H&alpha;]]-dim relative to their UV luminosity<ref name="halpha">Pflamm-Altenburg, J., Weidner, C., Kroupa, P. (2009). ''MNRAS'', 395, 394. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009MNRAS.395..394P</ref>
* Disk galaxies displaying radial H&alpha; cutoffs<ref name="nature2008">Pflamm-Altenburg, J., Kroupa, P. (2008). ''Nature'', 455, 641. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2008Natur.455..641P</ref>
* The mass-metallicity relation of galaxies<ref name="massmet">Köppen, J., Weidner, C., Kroupa, P. (2007). ''MNRAS'', 375, 673. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007MNRAS.375..673K</ref>
* The chemical enrichment histories of [[Elliptical galaxy|elliptical galaxies]]<ref name="elliptical">Recchi, S., Calura, F., Kroupa, P. (2009). ''A&A'', 499, 711. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A%26A...499..711R</ref>

In 2013 Kroupa and collaborators proposed that the stellar IMF represents an optimally sampled distribution function rather than a probability density distribution.<ref name="optimalimf">Kroupa, P. et al. (2013). In ''Stellar Systems and Galactic Structure'', Vol. 5, p. 115. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013pss5.book..115K/abstract</ref>

===Binary Stars and Star Cluster Dynamics===

Kroupa pioneered the treatment of an initial 100% binary fraction in stellar populations, working in part through interactions with [[N-body simulation]] developer Sverre Aarseth. His 1995 papers demonstrated that the lower binary fraction in the Galactic field (~50%) compared to young star-forming regions (~100%) results from dynamical disruption as clusters disperse.<ref name="mnras1995a">Kroupa, P. (1995). ''MNRAS'', 277, 1491. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1995MNRAS.277.1491K</ref> He also derived birth distribution functions of binary star periods, mass ratios, and eccentricities now used as standard inputs for population synthesis.<ref name="mnras1995b">Kroupa, P. (1995). ''MNRAS'', 277, 1507. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1995MNRAS.277.1507K</ref>

Extensions of this work produced predictions for stellar ejections from young clusters,<ref name="ejections">Oh, S., Kroupa, P. (2016). ''ApJ''. http://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08827</ref> new assessments of Cepheid populations,<ref name="cepheid">Dinnbier, F. et al. and Kroupa, P. (2024). Cepheid populations study. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A.385D/abstract</ref> and quantification of [[Stellar collision|stellar merger]] frequencies.<ref name="mergers">Dvorakova, N. et al. and Kroupa, P. (2024). Stellar merger frequencies. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...689A.234D/abstract</ref>

Research on tidal tails of open star clusters found an asymmetry in leading and trailing tails, which Kroupa and collaborators argue provides evidence for [[Milgromian dynamics]] on open cluster scales.<ref name="tidaltails">Kroupa, P. et al. (2022). ''MNRAS''. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022arXiv221013472K</ref><ref name="tidaltails2024">Kroupa, P., Pflamm-Altenburg, J., Mazurenko, S., Wu, W., Thies, I. et al. (2024). "Open Star Clusters and Their Asymmetrical Tidal Tails." ''ApJ'', 970, 94. doi:10.3847/1538-4357/ad4c66. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...970...94K/abstract</ref>

===Brown Dwarfs and Planetary Systems===

Kroupa's research demonstrated a statistical discontinuity between [[brown dwarf]]s and stars in the IMF. Together with Ingo Thies and Christian Theis, he proposed in 2003–2004 that brown dwarfs and extrasolar planetary systems may form in circumstellar disks disrupted by passing stars in dense embedded clusters.<ref name="browndwarfs">Thies, I., Kroupa, P., Theis, C. (2005). ''MNRAS'', 364, 961. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005MNRAS.364..961T</ref> Subsequent work proposed that such stellar encounters can also produce misaligned orbits and short-period eccentric exoplanets.<ref name="exoplanets">Thies, I., Kroupa, P., Goodwin, S.P. et al. (2010). ''ApJ'', 717, 577. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ApJ...717..577T</ref>

===Satellite Galaxies and the Plane of Satellites Problem===

In 1997 Kroupa presented stellar-dynamical models suggesting that the dwarf satellite galaxies of the Milky Way could be explained without invoking exotic dark matter.<ref name="dwarfsph">Kroupa, P. (1997). ''New Astronomy'', 2, 139. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1997NewA....2..139K</ref> He subsequently identified what is now known as the satellite galaxy plane problem: the eleven classical satellite galaxies of the [[Milky Way]] appear to lie in a thin disk — the Vast Polar Structure (VPOS) — which Kroupa and collaborators argue is statistically incompatible with the isotropic sub-halo distribution predicted by the ΛCDM model.<ref name="vpos">Pawlowski, M., Pflamm-Altenburg, J., Kroupa, P. (2012). ''MNRAS''. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012arXiv1204.5176P</ref>

This analysis was extended to show that satellite planes around both the Milky Way and Andromeda form a symmetrical structure.<ref name="localgroup">Pawlowski, M.S. et al. and Kroupa, P. (2013). Local Group symmetrical structure. ''MNRAS''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013MNRAS.435.1928P/abstract</ref>

A proposed explanation is that these satellites formed as tidal dwarf galaxies during a close encounter between the Milky Way and another galaxy approximately 10–11 Gyr ago, consistent with Milgromian dynamics.<ref name="tidalenc">Bilek, M., et al. (2018). Milky-Way–Andromeda encounter in MOND. ''A&A''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A%26A...614A..59B/abstract</ref><ref name="tidalenc2022">Banik, I., et al. (2022). Milky-Way–Andromeda encounter in MOND. ''MNRAS''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.513..129B/abstract</ref>

===Cosmological Tests and MOND===

Since approximately 2010, Kroupa's group has applied multiple independent observational tests to the ΛCDM cosmological model. These include:

* The El Gordo galaxy cluster test: the observed mass and collision velocity of the [[El Gordo cluster]] are argued to be incompatible with ΛCDM predictions.<ref name="elgordo">Asencio, E., Banik, I., Kroupa, P. (2021). El Gordo cluster test. ''MNRAS''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.500.5249A/abstract</ref>

* The KBC void test: the local underdensity of matter and associated galaxy bulk flows are argued to challenge ΛCDM, with Milgromian cosmological models proposed as an alternative and solving the [[Hubble tension]] self-consistently.<ref name="kbc">Haslbauer, M., Banik, I., Kroupa, P. (2020). KBC void and Hubble tension. ''MNRAS''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.2845H/abstract</ref><ref name="mazurenko2023">Mazurenko, S., Banik, I., Kroupa, P., Haslbauer, M. (2023). ''MNRAS''. https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17988</ref>

* The Fornax cluster dwarf galaxy test: the morphologies and distribution of [[Fornax Cluster|Fornax cluster]] dwarfs are argued to be inconsistent with ΛCDM predictions for dark matter halos.<ref name="fornax">Asencio, E., Banik, I., Mieske, S., Venhola, A., Kroupa, P., Zhao, H. (2022). ''MNRAS'', 515, 2981. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.515.2981A</ref>
* The Chandrasekhar dynamical friction test: Kroupa introduced this test and applied it to the [[Magellanic Clouds]]' motion about each other and past the Milky Way, arguing the result indicates the absence of a dark matter halo.<ref name="canjphys">Kroupa, P. (2015). ''Canadian Journal of Physics'', 93, 169. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015CaJPh..93..169K</ref><ref name="hernandez2025">Hernandez, X., Kroupa, P. (2025). "Dynamical Friction Constraints on the Dark Matter Hypothesis Across Astronomical Scales." ''Universe'', 11(11), 367. doi:10.3390/universe11110367. https://www.mdpi.com/2218-1997/11/11/367</ref>
* The galaxy-bar test: independently conducted work with Roshan et al. (2021) argued that observed galaxy bar rotation rates are inconsistent with [[Dark matter halo|dark matter halos]].<ref name="galaxybar">Roshan, M., et al. (2021). Galaxy-bar test. ''MNRAS''. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..926R/abstract</ref>

Kroupa led the development of the Phantom of Ramses (PoR) code for Milgromian galaxy simulations.<ref name="por">Lüghausen, F. et al. (2015); Nagesh, S.T. et al. (2021); Wittenburg, N. et al. (2023). Phantom of Ramses (PoR) code. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.498.5652K/abstract</ref>

His group has proposed the Bohemian Model of Cosmology as a possible framework addressing the Hubble tension, galaxy bulk flows, and the KBC void.<ref name="mazurenko2023"/>

Within the IGIMF theory framework, work by Eda Gjergo and Kroupa proposed that massive elliptical galaxies were far brighter when forming, around redshift 17, than today, with their formation contributing as a previously overlooked, non-negligible foreground component of the [[cosmic microwave background]] (CMB) — accounting for at least 1.4% and potentially up to the full present-day CMB energy density in some estimates.<ref name="gjergo2025">Gjergo, E., Kroupa, P. (2025). "The Impact of Early Massive Galaxy Formation on the Cosmic Microwave Background." ''Nuclear Physics B'', 1017, 116931. doi:10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2025.116931. https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025NuPhB101716931G/abstract</ref> A 2020 paper proposed a mechanism for the rapid early formation of super-massive black holes consistent with early [[quasar]] observations.<ref name="smbh">Kroupa, P. et al. (2020). Super-massive black hole formation. ''MNRAS''.</ref>

===Magellanic Clouds Proper Motions===

In 1994 and 1997, Kroupa and Ulrich Bastian published the first precise proper motion measurements of the [[Magellanic Clouds]] using [[Hipparcos]] data.<ref name="hipparcos">Kroupa, P., Bastian, U. (1997). ''New Astronomy'', 2, 77. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1997NewA....2...77K</ref>

===Star Formation and Galactic Structure===

Kroupa proposed modelling galaxies as systems where stars form in embedded star cluster populations rather than continuously from a smooth interstellar medium. This explained the age-related thickening of the Milky Way disk as a consequence of gas expulsion from embedded clusters, and predicted the Milky Way would have resembled a chain galaxy approximately 10 Gyr ago.<ref name="thickening">Kroupa, P. (2002). ''MNRAS'', 330, 707. http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002MNRAS.330..707K</ref><ref name="chaingalaxy">Zonoozi, A.H., Mahani, H., Kroupa, P. (2019). "Was the Milky Way a chain galaxy? Using the IGIMF theory to constrain the thin-disc star formation history and mass." ''MNRAS'', 483(1), 46–56. doi:10.1093/mnras/sty2812. https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/483/1/46/5144227</ref>

==Graduate Students and Research Group==

As of March 2026, Kroupa has successfully supervised 26 completed PhD students, with 9 currently enrolled (1 in Prague, 8 in Bonn).<ref name="cv"/> He has mentored one Habilitation. Two of his PhD students subsequently won Hubble Fellowships. The SPODYR group has hosted 10 Alexander von Humboldt Fellows, 1 Alexander von Humboldt Research Awardee, 1 Marie Curie Fellow, and 1 Heisenberg Fellow.<ref name="cv"/>

==Research Funding==

Kroupa has received grants from the DFG, Czech grant agencies, the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], and other bodies. Total third-party funding amounts to approximately 9 million Euro.<ref name="cv"/>
